title: Pre-Analysis — Acoustic Treatment of the Cabin Air Distribution System as First Proposed
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of the cabin air acoustic treatment as first submitted, covering the full riser and ceiling plenum run; the plenum half was rejected on fire load and clearance grounds and the scope reduced to the riser ducts.

sections.objective: Assess the acoustic treatment of the cabin air distribution system as first submitted, which lined the riser ducts and the ceiling plenum run, and establish whether the cabin fire load statement and the ceiling void clearances can carry it. The work order was raised internally after two years of passenger complaints about a tonal peak over the wing that the original duct design had not predicted.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the plenum half of the scope did not survive. The absorber material is a perforated facing over an open cell core, and the quantity proposed for the plenum run takes the cabin fire load above the value declared in the certification statement for the ceiling void. Reducing the quantity to fit takes the acoustic benefit below what was promised, so the plenum work was rejected rather than re-sized. In the riser ducts the treatment is clear on fire load but tight on clearance: the risers run through the same ceiling void as the aft equipment rack feeders, and the insert wall thickness leaves twelve millimetres to the feeder support.
sections.next_steps: Return the plenum half of the scope to the cabin office and re-submit the riser duct treatment alone. Fix the insert wall thickness at the value analysed rather than leaving it as a supplier option, so the clearance to the feeder support does not move. Re-issue the riser cleaning task with the insert in place, and confirm the fire load figure for the reduced scope with certification before release.

similarity_seeds: tonal peak in cabin air distribution noise over the wing
perforated absorber facing inside a distribution duct

tasks.title: Check the cabin fire load statement against the proposed quantity
Measure the ceiling void clearances on both airframes
Search installations sharing the ceiling void zones
Identify the cleaning content affected by an insert

expected_findings.rationale: The riser cleaning task uses a pressure wash that would strip a perforated facing and drive water into the open cell core. With an insert fitted the whole method changes, and there is no way to inspect the core once it is wet.
expected_findings.resolution: Task re-written for a dry method with a facing condition check; the wet method retained for unmodified ducts.

expected_findings.rationale: The riser run shares the ceiling void with the aft equipment rack feeders. With the insert wall thickness left as a supplier option the clearance to the feeder support can fall to five millimetres, which is below the installation rule for a duct against an electrical support.
expected_findings.resolution: Wall thickness fixed at the analysed value in the dossier rather than left to the supplier; clearance re-checked on both airframes.

expected_findings.rationale: The feeder sheet fixes the support spacing in the same void from a datum on the duct centre line. Nothing electrical changes, but the sheet note that quotes the duct outer diameter becomes wrong on a treated duct.
expected_findings.resolution: Sheet note re-worded to quote the support datum rather than the duct diameter.

expected_findings.rationale: Removing the aft secondary distribution box needs the same ceiling panels out. The access sequence would have had to name the treated duct as a handling caution if the plenum half of the scope had survived.
expected_findings.resolution: No action on the reduced scope; recorded in case the plenum treatment returns.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by similarity on shared cabin ceiling vocabulary and by the zone seed on 265 and 293, but it is a lighting change in the wall wash position outboard of the riser run and shares no part, no functional item number and no clearance case.

type_data.conclusion: Rejected as submitted. The riser duct treatment is sound and was re-submitted alone; the ceiling plenum treatment cannot be carried by the cabin fire load statement.
